column3: The Hebrew has a complete existence statement, “there was a man ... and his name”; BSB joins it to the next verse.
The Hebrew names silver without stating the shekel unit, and explicitly says “you cursed and also spoke in my ears”; BSB supplies the unit and condenses the hearing expression.
The Hebrew includes “from my hand” in the dedication; BSB omits that image and supplies the shekel unit.
The Hebrew ends with a singular “it was” in Micah’s house; BSB has plural “they were placed”. The shekel unit is supplied.
The shrine is literally a “house of God”, and ordination is described as filling the hand.
Judah is explicitly named twice, first with Bethlehem and then with the clan; BSB incorporates the second reference into the residence description.
The Hebrew names silver without a shekel unit and ends simply “the Levite went”; BSB supplies the unit and “in”.
The Hebrew explicitly calls him “the man”; BSB uses a pronoun and explicitly names Micah in the second clause.
Ordination is described as filling the Levite’s hand, and Micah’s name is repeated at the end; BSB uses “ordained” and “his house”.
